note: Generated by scripts/rules-from-prd.mjs; do not edit. stages = where Daniel may cite the rule; severity = default; allowed = what the review check accepts; condition = the PRD text that chooses between them.

rules.name: One message
rules.test: One conclusion, not two joined by "and"

rules.name: A finding, not a description
rules.test: States what the chart proves, not a list of facts, a label for what is plotted, or padding ("profitability varies widely")

rules.name: Full sentence
rules.test: Has a subject and a verb

rules.name: Real number
rules.test: Carries the key number where a real number sharpens the conclusion (a change, a gap, a CAGR); never an artificial one such as a 1–5 score. A qualitative conclusion without a number is fine

rules.name: Stands alone
rules.test: Makes sense without the chart or the speaker

rules.name: Answers the client's question
rules.test: Speaks to the stated audience's decision; a different client would need a different lead

rules.name: Insightful
rules.test: Not obvious or "motherhood": the audience would not say "we knew that"

rules.name: No overreach
rules.test: Goes no further than the chart shows: no motive, no "most", no action that needs more evidence than this chart

rules.name: Short
rules.test: Two lines at most; aim for 15 words or fewer

rules.name: Punch first
rules.test: Most important point first, then detail and qualifications; plain words, active verb, no hedging or wordy opener ("Looking at the data…")

rules.name: Follows from the data
rules.test: The chart can support it at all: no non-sequitur, no cause read from a correlation, no restating the client's belief without evidence

rules.name: No typos
rules.test: No spelling or grammar error in the lead

rules.name: Proves the lead
rules.test: Read as drawn, the data shows what the lead claims (a lead about revenue against football record needs the record on the chart)

rules.name: Right measure
rules.test: Plots the quantity the lead is about, not a proxy (salary uplift, not salary at graduation)

rules.name: Like-for-like
rules.test: Same base and start point; market growth, inflation or size removed where it distorts (index to the average)

rules.name: Enough comparators
rules.test: The comparison set can define "normal"

rules.name: Right span and window
rules.test: Covers the period the lead names, on both sides of any turning point; averaging windows chosen for a stated reason

rules.name: Lead's numbers on the chart
rules.test: Every number in the lead can be read off the chart, or is annotated on it

rules.name: Obtainable
rules.test: For a dummy chart, the data could realistically be obtained

rules.name: Robust
rules.test: A different reasonable choice (window, base, peer set) would not change the answer, or the page says so

rules.name: Honest gaps
rules.test: Missing data not filled or interpolated; coverage bias noted

rules.name: Lead's numbers right
rules.test: Every number in the lead matches the chart: same value, same measure, and any sum adds up (60 + 35 is not 90)

rules.name: Right broad type
rules.test: Numbers as a chart, never a pasted data table (that belongs in the appendix, for Q&A); ideas as a concept chart; text only for an argument

rules.name: Form fits the comparison
rules.test: Items: bar. Time: column or line. Distribution: histogram. Composition: stacked or 100% column, waterfall for change. Look for a better chart than a pie; never 3D

rules.name: Transformation exposes the lead
rules.test: Index, ratio, % change, a gap line, a CAGR: whichever makes the lead's comparison direct, so the reader never calculates

rules.name: One axis per measure
rules.test: No dual axes: they are rarely the best choice

rules.name: Emphasis
rules.test: What the lead names in colour, the rest grey

rules.name: Proof annotated
rules.test: Turning point, gap or gradient marked on the chart

rules.name: Relationship as an X-Y plot
rules.test: A relationship between two variables is one X-Y plot, points joined in time order and labelled at start, turning point and end; never two panels or a dual axis, because nobody can eyeball a relationship

rules.name: Log scale justified
rules.test: Only for wide ranges or growth rates, and labelled as log

rules.name: Panels
rules.test: One chart; two panels at most

rules.name: Lead numbers jump out
rules.test: Every number in the lead is highlighted on the chart in colour or size

rules.name: Growth as CAGR
rules.test: A time series shows the CAGR % for the period, per series at the right end or in the chart title, because nobody can eyeball a growth rate
rules.severityText: Major if the lead is about growth, else Minor
rules.condition: Major if the lead is about growth, else Minor

rules.name: Framework conventions
rules.test: A standard framework keeps its standard layout (GE matrix: market attractiveness vertical, competitive position horizontal)

rules.name: No typos on the chart
rules.test: No spelling or grammar error on the page outside the lead (typos in the lead are L12). Overrides the Common Module's "typo anywhere = hard stop" for this tool

rules.name: Source line
rules.test: Present, specific and accurate; Gen AI is never a source
rules.severityText: Hard stop; Major for a dummy chart (say where the data will come from) or a source that is present but wrong
rules.condition: Hard stop; Major for a dummy chart (say where the data will come from) or a source that is present but wrong

rules.name: Standard template
rules.test: Lead as the title; chart title states what the data is, its unit, period and CAGR where relevant; data; source. Keys such as bubble size go in a legend, not the title

rules.name: No noise
rules.test: No data that does not serve the lead; no gridlines, borders, shadows or decoration; 3D looks unprofessional

rules.name: No duplication
rules.test: Data labels or a value axis, not both (drop the axis); series labelled beside their line or segment, not in a legend

rules.name: Digestible numbers
rules.test: Rounded (to HK$m, or to the nearest 10); consistent decimals; short axis labels (08/09)

rules.name: Labels and units
rules.test: Every axis, unit and series identifiable; no bare numbers ("3100; 37%")

rules.name: Aligned and consistent
rules.test: Elements aligned; one font; consistent sizes; six colours at most

rules.name: Plain wording
rules.test: Short labels, no jargon or abbreviations

rules.name: Readable
rules.test: No text below 12pt

rules.name: Dummy-chart label
rules.test: Dummy data marked "Illustrative data"

rules.name: Engaging
rules.test: Optional: one device that helps the reader engage without adding noise

rules.name: Reference lines labelled
rules.test: Dotted and average lines say what they mark

rules.name: 10-second test
rules.test: A senior reader gets the lead from the planned chart in 10 seconds

rules.name: Lead matches the chart's shape
rules.test: A time-series chart carries a lead about change; a ranking chart, a lead about rank

rules.name: Same measure
rules.test: After a transformation, the lead's number uses the chart's measure (an index, not £m)

rules.name: Emphasis on the lead
rules.test: Colour and annotations fall on what the lead names (numbers: C10)

rules.name: Still no overreach
rules.test: L8 and L11 rechecked against the planned chart

rules.name: Storyline or appendix
rules.test: A weak lead or a data table marks an appendix page, kept for Q&A; the EM says so
